subject.title: fix(memory): recover real on-disk path for slugified QMD search results

question: Should QMD reads remain restricted to exact active indexed paths, or may a unique slug-equivalent inactive filesystem path become an authorized canonical document?
rationale: The PR changes a shipped workspace-read security invariant, and code review cannot choose that permanent authorization contract without Memory/QMD owner intent.

options.title: Canonicalize before search
options.body: Build a bounded realpath-checked alias map during collection refresh and authorize only the resulting prepared canonical paths.

options.title: Approve alias-equivalent reads
options.body: Explicitly adopt slug-equivalent inactive files as authorized documents, with collision, symlink, containment, performance, and native-QMD proof before merge.

options.title: Wait for native QMD
options.body: Pause this mitigation and require the native QMD indexer to keep real filesystem paths active so OpenClaw retains exact-path reads.

recommendation.title: Canonicalize before search
recommendation.body: Build a bounded realpath-checked alias map during collection refresh and authorize only the resulting prepared canonical paths.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice changes a shipped memory_get security boundary and requires the strongest available reviewer connected to recent memory-core release decisions.
